blocks.text: A bakery in Ibadan needs a plot of ground, bakers to knead and bake, ovens and mixers, and somebody willing to risk her savings on the whole venture. Remove any one of the four and the bread never appears. Economists call them the factors of production.

blocks.markdown:
**Production** is the creation of goods and services to satisfy human wants. It includes not only manufacturing but also transport, wholesaling, retailing, banking and teaching — anything that adds utility.

Every act of production requires inputs, and economists group all inputs into four **factors of production**, each with its own reward.

rows: All free gifts of nature — the soil, mineral deposits, rivers, forests, sunlight, fisheries
All human effort, physical and mental, applied to production
All man-made assets used to produce further goods — machinery, buildings, tools, stock, money for investment
The person who organises the other three factors and bears the risk of the enterprise
blocks.caption: The four factors of production and their rewards — learn these pairings exactly

items: **Land** is fixed in total supply, geographically immobile, a free gift of nature, heterogeneous in quality, and subject to the law of diminishing returns.

**Labour** cannot be separated from the labourer, is perishable because an unworked hour is lost forever, is both geographically and occupationally mobile in varying degrees, and its supply depends on the size and structure of the population.
**Capital** is man-made, comes out of savings and therefore out of forgone present consumption, depreciates with use, and is demanded not for itself but for what it produces.

**The entrepreneur** organises the other factors, takes the decisions, bears uninsurable risk and uncertainty, and is a residual claimant — profit is what remains after every other factor has been paid, and it may be negative.

blocks.title: Efficiency of labour
blocks.text: The efficiency of labour is the output a worker produces per unit of time. It depends on education and training, health and nutrition, the level of wages, the quality of capital equipment available, the standard of management and the conditions of work. Two workers with identical hours can differ greatly in output for these reasons.

blocks.markdown:
### Division of labour and specialisation

**Division of labour** is the splitting of a production process into separate tasks, each performed by a different worker. **Specialisation** is the concentration of a worker, a firm, a region or a country on the activity it does best. Adam Smith illustrated the idea in *The Wealth of Nations* in 1776 with his famous pin factory, where dividing the making of a pin into separate operations raised output enormously.

**Advantages**: total output rises; skill improves through repetition; time is saved because workers do not move between tasks; the use of machinery becomes worthwhile; unit costs fall; and training a worker for one task is quicker and cheaper.

**Disadvantages**: work becomes monotonous and workers lose pride in the finished article; craftsmanship declines; heavy interdependence means one stoppage halts the whole line; a highly specialised worker is occupationally immobile and vulnerable if the industry closes; and the risk of technological unemployment increases.

**Limitations**: the size of the market — you cannot subdivide a process if only ten units are sold a week; the nature of the product, since some goods cannot be broken into tasks; the indivisibility of certain processes; and the level of technology and management skill available.

blocks.title: Matching factors and rewards in a real business
blocks.prompt: Mrs Okonkwo rents a shop for ₦600,000 a year, borrows ₦2,000,000 from a bank at 15 per cent, employs three tailors at ₦80,000 each per month, and keeps whatever is left. Her revenue last year was ₦6,000,000 and materials cost ₦1,500,000. Identify the factor payments and calculate her profit.

steps.text: Land: the shop rent of ₦600,000 is the reward to land.
Capital: interest on the loan is 15 per cent of ₦2,000,000 = ₦300,000.

Entrepreneur: profit is the residual. ₦6,000,000 − ₦5,280,000 = ₦720,000. Note that if revenue had been ₦5,000,000 the residual would have been negative — which is exactly what it means to say the entrepreneur bears the risk.

blocks.answer: Rent ₦600,000, interest ₦300,000, wages ₦2,880,000, and profit to the entrepreneur ₦720,000

blocks.title: Money is not capital in the economist's sense
blocks.text: In everyday speech people call cash capital. In economics, capital means produced means of production — machines, buildings, tools, stocks. Money becomes capital only when it is used to acquire those assets. Examiners set this trap frequently, so state the distinction explicitly.

points: Production is the creation of goods and services that satisfy wants, including services as well as manufacturing.
The four factors are land, labour, capital and the entrepreneur, rewarded by rent, wages, interest and profit respectively.
Land is fixed and immobile; labour is perishable and inseparable from the worker; capital is man-made and comes from savings.
The entrepreneur bears risk and is a residual claimant, so profit can be negative.
Division of labour raises output and skill and lowers unit cost, but causes monotony, interdependence and occupational immobility.
The main limitation on division of labour is the size of the market.
